blocks.body:
## Technical summary

**Outcome: corrected and build-safe.** The audit assessed all **8,741** questions in the ages 11–17 and adult Layperson boundary. Before reallocation, ages 11–17 were **15 points harder at the median**. After balanced two-way swaps, the Layperson median is **18 points higher**. Exactly **1,911 questions moved each way**, both audience sizes are unchanged, and Layperson remains **16 adult-content points below Deacon**.

## Key findings

The inversion was structural. Of the teen questions moved to Layperson, **957** require identifying a Bible book from an unattributed passage, **610** require an exact missing word, and **340** require classifying an unattributed passage by canon section. By contrast, all **1,400 word-recognition** questions and all **533 familiar story-context** questions remained in ages 11–17. Only **4 of 118 hand-written teen trivia** questions moved, so the curated trivia was not the problem.

## Scope and definitions

The population is the complete union of the **6,667** ages 11–17 questions and **2,074** adult Layperson questions after the existing adult-difficulty audit. Ages 4–10, Deacon, and Pastor questions were not candidates for this move. ‘Before’ is reconstructed from repository source banks plus the frozen adult difficulty manifest, so rerunning the analysis does not depend on a mutable shipping snapshot. ‘After’ changes audience metadata only; stable question IDs, support numbers, wording, choices, answers, explanations, and categories are preserved.

## Methodology

Each question receives a label-independent **0–100 readiness score** from canonical knowledge (30), task abstraction (25), reading burden (20), answer specificity (15), and distractor competitiveness (10). Higher scores indicate more independent Bible-study skill and therefore stronger adult readiness. Allocation ranks the combined pool while preserving its original audience sizes. An adult-content ceiling of **53** prevents a question from entering Layperson when doing so would compress the next Layperson-to-Deacon boundary. Deterministic tie-breakers favor the original audience to minimize churn.

## Safeguards and edge cases

Every question moved into ages 11–17 has four choices and passes the existing archaic, sexual-content, and graphic-wording screen. **15** records were locked adult-only by that screen. After the primary rank allocation, **148** category-floor swaps preserved at least **20** adult Layperson questions in every category. The full adult audit then passed with medians **42 → 58 → 80**, zero manifest mismatch, and zero allocation drift.

## Limitations and uncertainty

**Confidence is high for reproducibility and population ordering, and medium for individual pedagogical placement.** This is a deterministic editorial cold-start model, not an item-response study. It cannot observe reading fluency, church background, denomination, ambiguity, or real answer rates. Tail overlap remains possible because audience size, safety, category availability, and the adjacent Deacon safeguard are hard constraints. Those exceptions are documented per question in the CSV and frozen manifest rather than hidden.

## Recommendations

Ship this corrected boundary, then collect anonymous correctness rate, response time, skip rate, and age-band selection for each stable question ID. Re-estimate placement after a useful sample is available, using response-rate bands and differential performance by audience as the primary evidence. Editorially review the lowest-confidence cutoff cases first, then inspect questions with unexpectedly high teen failure or unexpectedly high Layperson success.

## Traceability

The shipping iOS and Android banks are byte-identical. `audience_overrides.json` freezes all **3,822** audience changes by stable question ID. `all_questions.csv` contains every component score and decision; `changes.csv` contains every move; `summary.json` reconciles counts and distributions; and the executed notebook reproduces the headline checks from those outputs.

UNION ALL
